training_data: ADNI autopsy subsample (derivation): 75 AD-pathology participants with ante-mortem MRI at MCI/mild dementia (36 'pure' AD, 39 AD+); cortex-to-hippocampus GM ratio and cut-off 0.858 set by ROC (AUC 0.79)
test_data: Other ADNI participants not in the derivation cohort: 224 MCI and 221 mild dementia with CSF evidence of AD; classified by the fixed cut-off and compared on cognition and progression (no pathology labels, so no classification accuracy)
reason: Both the derivation and the validation cohorts come from ADNI, so the validation is a disjoint subset of the same consortium, not an external institution; under the template's train/test-split rule this is V3. The validation cohort has no neuropathology, so it tests prognostic associations of the fixed cut-off rather than classification accuracy, which the authors list as a limitation.

quotes.quote: We used the subsample of ADNI participants who had undergone post-mortem neuropathological examinations to identify atrophy patterns indicative of ‘pure’ AD or mixed pathology.

To validate the utility of the MRI measures derived from the derivation cohort, ADNI patients at the stage of MCI (n = 224) and mild dementia (n = 221) with CSF markers indicative of AD pathology [17], who were not part of the derivation cohort, were selected as the validation cohort.

Based on this cut-off for the cortex-to-hippocampus ratio, patients of the in vivo validation cohort were classified into two groups: a ‘pure’ AD-classified group with a ratio below, and an AD+-classified group with a ratio above the cut-off.
a reproduction of the classification accuracy of the cortex-to-hippocampus ratio in a separate post-mortem sample would strengthen the case for the pathological correlates of this measure.
